title: Why AI food looks like that
slides: Why do AI food images look strangely perfect?
Training data skews toward glossy, appetizing stock photos.
AI never tasted food, so it optimizes for visual appeal.
Now you can spot fakes by checking for weird reflections.
Next time you see one, zoom in—and question realism.
thread_text:
1. Why so perfect?

AI food images are trained on stock photos, not real meals. The result: a glow that never exists in your kitchen.

2. The missing taste

AI has never eaten. It can't know that burnt edges or uneven sauces are natural, so it smooths them into fantasy.

3. Spot the fake

Check reflections on glasses or cutlery. AI often renders them physically impossible—a clue that the image is fabricated.

4. The realism trap

Your brain is wired to prefer these flawless images, making you more likely to engage. That's the hidden danger.

5. Take a closer look

Next time a food pic stops your scroll, zoom in. Are the highlights real? If not, question what else is fake.

instagram.caption:
That glossy burger you just scrolled past? It never existed — and the AI that made it has never tasted one. 🍔

AI food visuals are built from stock photos, not real meals. Since the software has no sense of taste, it polishes everything into a shiny, impossibly perfect version of food. It even removes natural flaws like burnt edges or uneven sauce.

Now, that polish is becoming a problem you can spot: check reflections on glasses or cutlery. AI often renders them physically impossible.

For anyone creating food content, this means your benchmark for "real" just shifted — and your audience might trust you more for showing imperfections.

Next time a perfect dish stops your scroll, zoom in. Are those highlights real? 🔍
